title: Insights
intro: Your training load and trends, computed from the runs you logged.

period.partial: Partial period: data through {{date}} ({{elapsed}} of {{days}} days).

errors.toBeforeFrom: The end date must not be before the start date.
errors.tooLong: A period can be at most 366 days.

compare.label: Compare with
compare.noComparison: No comparison is available for this period.

planned.title: Planned
planned.none: No planned runs in this period.
planned.missed: {{count}} missed (planned before today and not completed)

acwr.title: Load change vs your recent norm
acwr.label: Acute:chronic workload ratio

band.low: Low: your last 7 days were lighter than your recent norm.
band.optimal: Optimal: your last 7 days were in line with your recent norm.
band.high: High: your last 7 days were heavier than your recent norm.

acwr.chronic: Recent norm (4 weeks before, per week)
acwr.insufficientHistory: Available after {{days}} days of logged training; {{logged}} so far.
acwr.noChronicLoad: There was no logged training in the 4 weeks before the last 7 days, so there is nothing to compare with.
acwr.bandDays: Days in this period: {{low}} low, {{optimal}} optimal, {{high}} high, {{unavailable}} without a ratio.
acwr.means: The ratio compares your training load of the last 7 days with the weekly average of the 4 weeks before. It shows how much your load changed compared with your recent norm.
acwr.not: It does not predict injury and it is not medical advice. A high or low value only says that this week looked different from your recent weeks.
acwr.thresholds: Bands: low below {{low}}, optimal {{low}} to {{high}}, high above {{high}}.

monotony.title: Weekly monotony
monotony.uniform: Your days looked alike that week, with little difference between hard and easy days.
monotony.varied: Your days differed between hard and easy that week.
monotony.unavailable: Not available for that week: it needs training on at least two days with different load.
monotony.noWeek: Not available yet: there is no complete week in this period.
monotony.explain: Monotony is the average daily load divided by its day-to-day variation; strain is the weekly load times monotony. Values above {{high}} mean a week without much variety compared with your usual pattern. This describes the week, it does not predict injury.

empty.title: No completed runs in this period
empty.body: Log a run or pick another period to see totals and charts.

quality.title: About these numbers
quality.estimated: {{share}} of the training load comes from {{count}} sessions without a logged effort (RPE); a typical effort for the run type was used. Log RPE for more accurate load.
quality.noDuration: {{count}} sessions have no duration and count as zero load.
quality.noDistance: {{count}} runs have no distance and are left out of distance and pace.

volume.plannedNote: Hatched bars are planned runs not yet completed.
volume.summaryWeek: Highest week: {{label}} with {{value}}; average {{average}} per week over {{total}} weeks.
volume.summaryMonth: Highest month: {{label}} with {{value}}; average {{average}} per month over {{total}} months.

loadChart.title: Acute and chronic load
loadChart.summary: On {{date}} the acute load was {{acute}} and the chronic load {{chronic}}.
loadChart.summaryNoChronic: On {{date}} the acute load was {{acute}}; there is no chronic load yet.
loadChart.chronic: Chronic (weekly average of the 4 weeks before)

acwrChart.title: Load change over time
acwrChart.summary: On {{date}} the ratio was {{value}} ({{band}}). It was low on {{low}} days, optimal on {{optimal}} and high on {{high}}.

types.title: Time by run type
types.summary: {{label}} took the largest share of your time: {{share}} of {{time}}.

pace.title: Easy-run pace
pace.summaryFaster: Easy-run pace got faster by {{amount}} per week on average.
pace.summarySlower: Easy-run pace got slower by {{amount}} per week on average.
pace.summaryFlat: Easy-run pace stayed about the same.
pace.notEnough: Not enough weeks with easy runs for a trend; it needs at least 4.
pace.none: No easy runs in this period. The trend uses runs of the type Easy run on roads and tracks; trail runs and very short runs are left out.
pace.excluded: {{count}} easy runs were left out (trail surface, under 1 km or an unusual pace).
pace.fasterIsUp: Pace in min/km; faster is higher on the chart.

races.title: Race results
